newsitem.title: GERMANY: German orders rise points to moderate 97 growth.
newsitem.headline: German orders rise points to moderate 97 growth.

text.p: German industrial orders rose 0.5 percent in November on a seasonally adjusted basis, driven by solid gains in domestic capital goods orders and in eastern Germany, the economics ministry said on Tuesday.
The modest uptrend shown in November orders followed a 2.7 percent climb in the index in October, reversing a 3.3 percent fall in September.
Economists said the November figures confirmed estimates of moderate economic growth in 1997, and reinforced expectations of no change in interest rates.

"We expect gross domestic product to show real growth of two percent in 1997 after 1.3 percent in 1996," said Trinkaus Capital Management in a research note. "The Bundesbank has no economic need to change interest rates."
Earlier on Tuesday Germany research institute DIW lowered its forecast for 1997 growth to two percent from an earlier prediction of 2.5 percent.
Orders in east Germany rose 5.6 percent from the previous month, while in west Germany they were up 0.2 percent.
For the country as a whole, domestic capital goods orders jumped 4.1 percent. Foreign capital goods orders rose 0.3 percent in November.
"The strength of domestic orders provided the good news, but foreign orders, although still rising, seem to have lost a little momentum," said Stephen King, an HSBC James Capel economist in London.

Orders for consumer goods were unchanged in November, while intermediate goods orders fell 0.8 percent. "This is evidence of a continued pickup in manufacturing output -- but not necessarily in final demand," King said.
November orders were 3.6 percent higher than in the year-earlier month. In west Germany they rose 5.5 percent year-on-year, while in the east they were down 21.8 percent.
